headline: Council approves cell tower easement, airport master plan, union contract, and homeland security grant; rejects executive session.
summary: The council approved disposition of 12 Fair Street, called a public hearing on Charter amendments, approved an easement agreement for a cell tower site, and supported the Auburn-Lewiston Airport Master Plan. It also approved a collective bargaining agreement with the Maine Service Employees Association and accepted a $190,000 Homeland Security grant. A motion to enter executive session to discuss a legal matter did not pass.
decisions: Accepted and placed on file the minutes of the meetings of August 18, 25, and 26, 2026.
Cancelled the November 3, 2026 City Council meeting and set one regular meeting for November 17.
Approved the disposition of 12 Fair Street to Baxter Homes, LLC for $49,900.
Called for a public hearing on proposed City Charter amendments to be held September 15.
Approved an easement agreement with TPA VIII, LLC for the cell tower site at 532 East Avenue.
Approved supporting implementation of the Auburn-Lewiston Municipal Airport Master Plan and Five-Year Sponsor Commitment.
Authorized the City Administrator to execute a three-year collective bargaining agreement with the Maine Service Employees Association.
Accepted and appropriated the FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Award of $190,000.
Motion to enter executive session to discuss a legal matter with the City Attorney did not pass.

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 7:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Roy, Noble, Chittim, 
and Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and 
City Clerk Kathleen Montejo.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (311-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meetings of August 18, 25 and 26, 2026, and 
to accept and place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Amy Sussman, Bar Harbor – Nephew was killed in the mass shooting, wants to know what 
happened to the money promised to them by the Maine Community Foundation. Lewiston non-
profits made out well with money raised and promised to victims’ families and survivors. This 
issue is clearly not a priority for this Council. The Maine Mill received $65,000. The Mayor is on 
their board of directors and should have disclosed this conflict of interest. A survivor attended 
their grand opening and was surprised by the memorial.   
 
Amy Smith, 122 Bartlett St – The Healthy Neighborhoods association held their annual Bulky 
Waste Removal program, 102 tons were removed.  September 11 is the next event.  
 
Joe Philippon, Ward 1 – L/A Arts held the Art Walk on Friday night and a band that set up in 
Courthouse Plaza was not allowed to use the city’s electrical power outlet.  It is unfortunate the 
city does not support these events and the local arts. The band had to bring in a generator. These 
events bring in hundreds of people into the downtown. 
 
Ronnie Paradis, Ward 6 – Sunday’s newspaper featured a story about a public high school in 
Fort Kent that is dedicated to treating recovering addicts who are high school students.  
Lewiston should dedicate some of the opioid settlement funds for a local public school program. 
Need a public health coordinator for this city.  Loneliness is a national crisis and there are many 
people in this city not connected to the community.  Seniors are lonely. We need to support each 
other more. 
 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 –  There was very limited public notice for the special meeting on 
Wednesday, August 26.  He received the email notice at 12:16pm for the 6pm meeting. This is 
an example of why people think the Council operations are shady.  The Housing Committee 
should have been at the Council meeting to answer questions.
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
2 
 
Andrew Jones, Ward 2 –  Owes an apology to the Council, made an unprofessional gesture 
when leaving the Council Chambers at the last meeting, wants to hold himself accountable 
because he calls on the Mayor and Council to hold themselves accountable, so he apologized for 
his actions. The Housing Committee did not request that the moratorium on the mobile home lot 
rents be extended and committee members say the chair is withholding information. The process 
is tainted and should start over. 
 
Lisa Jones, Ward 2 – Lewiston Housing received $65,000 from the Maine Community 
Foundation funds raised for the mass shooting victims. Craig Saddlemire’s organization received 
$65,000 from this same fund as well.. They need to be directed to return the money.  
 
Jay Rodrigue, Ward 6 – The City is not helping or supporting small businesses. The mobile 
home parks should not be told what to charge for lot rents. The city cannot control the expenses 
of a business and they should not control the revenue.  Need more businesses here but need to 
support them. 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
The Fire Department will be holding a service on Friday, Sept 11 at 8:30am to commemorate the 
25th anniversary of the September 11 attack on this country. A featured speaker will be a family 
member of one of the six Mainers who passed away in one of the plane crashes; the deceased 
was raised in Lewiston.  Friday, September 4 is the home owning game of the LHS football 
team under the direction of their new coach, Justin Bisson who works at Public Works.  Thank 
you to everyone who worked at the Balloon Festival; balloons were able to launch during three 
of the scheduled six slots. The Central Avenue project for a new water main should be done by 
the end of this month.  
 
The City is undertaking a marketing rebranding and conducting a survey that should take 7-9 
minutes to complete; residents are encouraged to complete it. The sound barrier panels at the 
North Temple Pickleball Courts were scheduled to be installed today but there was an 
unexpected delay so Public Works hopes to have these installed soon. The Lewiston Maineiacs 
hockey team is back at The Colisee and their home opener is Sept 13.  Lewiston Economic 
Development is offering small business loans, if interested, please see the website for more 
information,  The fall Recreation programs offer a great variety from tenn is to archery to salsa 
dancing. The decisions on the reorganization of the departments on the Third Floor is complete – 
Economic Development will become a division of City Administration and Community 
Development will be its own department with expanded duties.  
 
ADOPTION OF MEETING SCHEDULE FOR THE MONTH OF NOVEMBER 
 
VOTE (312-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To suspend Section 2.4 of the Rules Governing the City Council and cancel the November 3, 
2026 City Council meeting due to the conflict with Election Day and to hold one regular meeting 
during the month of November on Tuesday, November 17th.   Passed - Vote 7-0
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
3 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE DISPOSITION OF 12 FAIR STREET 
 
VOTE (313-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve the Order, Approving the Disposition of 12 Fair Street: 
 
Whereas, the City Council voted to sell the tax acquired parcel located at 12 Fair Street at their  
7/15/2025 meeting and 
 
Whereas, the City received an offer for the parcel through the City’s Realtor DuBois Realty; and 
 
Whereas, Baxter Homes, LLC offered $49,900 for 12 Fair Street  
 
Now, Therefore, B e It Ordered by the C ity Council of the C ity of L ewiston, to approve the 
disposition of 12 Fair Street and authorize the City Administrator to execute all necessary legal 
documents to include Lewiston’s retainage of utility easements for the parcel. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, CALLING FOR A PUBLIC HEARING FOR THE PROPOSED 
CITY CHARTER AMENDMENTS 
 
VOTE (314-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve the Order, Calling for a Public Hearing for the proposed City Charter amendments: 
 
Whereas, The City Council has authorized over the past few months three amendments to the 
City Charter to appear on the November ballot, and 
Whereas, Maine state statutes require a public hearing to be held before election day regarding 
the amendments, and 
Whereas, The statutes require a legal advertisement to run at least seven days before the public 
hearing,  
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council that the City Council calls for a public 
hearing on the proposed Charter amendments to be held on September 15 and directs city staff to 
place the necessary legal notice as prescribed by state statutes.  
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
RESOLUTION, APPROVING AN EASEMENT AGREEMENT WITH TPA IX, LLC 
FOR A CELL TOWER SITE AT 532 EAST AVENUE 
 
Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley provided background information for this item.
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
4 
 
VOTE (315-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
  
To approve the Resolution, Approving an Easement Agreement with TPA IX, LLC for a Cell 
Tower Site at 532 East Avenue: 
 
Whereas, pursuant to the provisions of Charter the City of Lewiston, Maine has the authority to 
purchase, lease, receive, hold and enjoy real property and further have the authority to control, 
lease, sublease, convey, or otherwise dispose of real property; and 
 
Whereas, the City Administrator is granted the authority to sign all written contracts entered into 
by the City and the authority to sign all conveyances made by the City; further the City Council 
is authorized to acknowledge the execution of all instruments executed by the City which 
required acknowledgment; and 
 
Whereas, on the 1st day of September 2026, the City Council of the City of Lewiston, Maine 
approved the sale of its interest in a telecommunications lease agreement with SBA 
Communications to Tower Point Acquisitions, LLC, and authorized the City Administrator to 
enter negotiations with Tower Point to finalize the sale by granting an Easement Agreement as to 
the City’s interest in the existing cell tower site (“the site”) located at 532 East Avenue, 
Lewiston, Maine 04240; and 
 
Whereas, the City Administrator has negotiated the terms of an Easement Agreement for the site 
and has executed a Letter of Intent dated August 18, 2026, with Tower Point Acquisitions, LLC, 
to transfer the City’s interest in the site to TPA VIII, LLC. 
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Hereby Resolved and Ordered By The City Council of The City of 
Lewiston, Maine, as follows: 
 
 Section 1.  The City Council of the City of Lewiston, Maine hereby approves the 
execution of an Easement Agreement by and between the City of Lewiston, Maine and TPA 
VIII, LLC, a Delaware Limited Liability Company, in the form presented. 
 
 Section 2.  The City Administrator of the City of Lewiston, Maine, is hereby authorized 
to execute said Easement Agreement on behalf of the City of Lewiston. 
 
 Section 3.  The City Administrator of the City of Lewiston, Maine, is hereby authorized 
to execute on behalf of the City of Lewiston, Maine all closing documents required to close the 
transaction described in the Easement Agreement and the Letter of Intent. 
 
Section 4.  The provisions of this Resolution shall become effective immediately upon 
adoption. 
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Resolved by the City Council of the City of Lewiston, Maine, that this  
Resolution be adopted in its entirety. 
 
Passed - Vote 5-2 (Councilors Chittim and Nagine opposed)
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
5 
 
ORDER, SUPPORTING IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AUBURN-LEWISTON 
MUNICIPAL AIRPORT MASTER PLAN AND FIVE-YEAR  
SPONSOR COMMITMENT 
 
Airport Manager Jonathan LaBonte and Airport Board member Mark Blais of Lewiston made a 
presentation to the Council regarding the Airport’s Master Plan. 
 
VOTE (316-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve the Order, Supporting Implementation of the Auburn -Lewiston Municipal Airport 
Master Plan and Five-Year Sponsor Commitment: 
 
Whereas, under the Federal Surplus Property Act of 1944, the Cities of Auburn and Lewiston 
accepted transfer of the Auburn-Lewiston Municipal Airport from the United States and accepted 
the restrictions, covenants, and obligations associated with that transfer; and 
Whereas, in 1979, the Cities of Auburn and Lewiston entered into an Interlocal Agreement 
establishing the Auburn -Lewiston Municipal Airport Board for the purpose of operating, 
maintaining, and improving the Auburn-Lewiston Municipal Airport, providing air transportation 
service for Auburn, Lewiston, and the surrounding region, and supporting industrial, 
manufacturing, and business development at the Airport and Industrial Airpark; and 
Whereas, the Interlocal Agreement delegates management of Airport property, facilities, leases, 
accounts, revenues, operations, and related assets to the Airport Board on behalf of the two 
municipal sponsors; and 
Whereas, the Auburn-Lewiston Municipal Airport is a federally obligated public -use airport, and 
continued sponsorship carries obligations related to safe and serviceable operation, airport 
property management, compatible land use, proper use of airport revenue, g rant compliance, and 
preservation of the Airport for airport purposes; and 
Whereas, in 2022, the FAA New England Compliance Office conducted a Land Use Inspection of 
the Airport and identified a significant number of compliance violations relating to property 
management, revenue diversion, and leases, some of which had been in place for  more than two 
decades; and 
Whereas, in 2025, the Airport completed its FAA-approved Corrective Action Plan, but continuing 
sponsor commitments remain for obstruction removal, wildlife management, updating the Exhibit 
“A” property record, and maintaining long -term compliance with federal ob ligations under the 
Grant Assurances; and 
Whereas, in order to be offered the FAA grants associated with the T-hangar construction project, 
the Airport was required to commit to the removal of approximately 2,700 obstructions within a 
defined period, with future FAA funding at risk if that commitment is not met; and 
Whereas, the Airport has completed a new Airport Master Plan and Airport Layout Plan to guide 
the next phase of airport compliance, capital investment, obstruction mitigation, aviation
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
6 
 
development, non-aeronautical revenue development, compatible land -use protection, and long -
term sustainability; and 
Whereas, implementation of the Master Plan requires clear, timely, and binding sponsor direction 
over the next five-year period, including local grant match for FAA entitlement and discretionary 
funding, pavement and capital repair, obstruction mitigation, wildli fe management, property and 
title documentation, operational support, and protection of Airport revenues and assets for Airport 
purposes, and delay in that direction places FAA grant eligibility, obstruction mitigation deadlines, 
and both Cities' compliance standing at risk; 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the Lewiston City Council as follows: 
1. Master Plan Support 
The Council supports implementation of the Auburn-Lewiston Municipal Airport Master Plan and 
Airport Layout Plan as the planning framework for Airport safety, compliance, capital investment, 
aviation development, revenue development, compatible land -use pr otection, and long -term 
sustainability. 
2. Independent Effect of Adoption 
The commitments and directions in this Order, including support for the Master Plan and 
participation in the five-year implementation plan take effect upon adoption of this Order by either 
City Council and are not contingent upon adoption of this Order by the other Airport Sponsor. 
3. Five-Year Implementation Plan 
The Airport Board, Airport Director, Auburn City Manager, and the Lewiston City Administrator 
and/or his designee, are directed to prepare a five -year Airport implementation plan for Fiscal 
Years 2028 through 2032. 
The plan shall identify major capital projects, FAA and MaineDOT  grant opportunities, required 
local match, obstruction mitigation needs, wildlife management commitments, Exhibit “A” and 
property documentation needs, state -of-good-repair priorities, operating support assumptions, 
revenue-development opportunities, and required sponsor actions. The plan shall be completed 
and presented to both Councils no later than November 30th, 2026. 
4. Sponsor Commitment and Protection of Airport Revenue 
The Council affirms that continued sponsorship of the Airport requires active, timely, and 
adequately funded support for the Airport's federal and state obligations, including safe and 
serviceable operation, local grant match, obstruction mitigation, wildl ife management, capital 
renewal, airport property documentation, compatible land -use protection, and preservation of 
Airport revenue for Airport purposes. 
 
Passed - Vote 5-2 (Councilors Roy and Martel opposed)
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
7 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO EXECUTE A 
COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENT WITH THE MAINE SERVICE 
EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION 
 
VOTE (317-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing the City Administrator to Execute a Collective Bargaining 
Agreement with the Maine Service Employees Association: 
 
Whereas, The City has been in recent discussion with the Maine Service Employees Association;  
and 
 
Whereas, all who participated in the development of the Maine Service Employees Association  
Collective Bargaining Agreement believe that negotiations have produced a contract which is  
sensitive to the current economic climate and reflects the organizational goals and objectives of  
both the city and the Maine Service Employees Association; and 
 
Whereas, as a result, the City’s negotiators and union representatives have reached a tentative  
agreement on a three-year contract covering the City’s FY27 through FY29; 
 
Now, therefore, be it ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston that 
The City Administrator is hereby authorized to execute a three -year collective bargaining 
agreement with the Maine Service Employees Association reflecting the attached terms and 
conditions. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, ACCEPTING AND APPROPRIATING THE FY2025 HOMELAND SECURITY 
GRANT AWARD OF $190,000 
 
VOTE (318-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve the Order, Accepting and Appropriating the FY2025 Homeland Security Grant 
Award of $190,000: 
 
Whereas, annually the City, along with area agencies submits a Homeland Security Grant  
application to request funding for various qualified public safety initiatives and equipment; and 
 
Whereas, requested projects in this grant year include COBRA Team funding and a mobile  
surveillance trailer; and  
 
Whereas, utilizing federally funding for these various public safety needs reduces the impact on  
the municipal tax rates;  
 
Now, therefore, be it Ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston that
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
8 
 
The FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Award of $190,000.00 is hereby accepted and appropriated.  
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
UPDATE REGARDING PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO THE 
SOLID WASTE ORDINANCE 
 
Director of Planning & Code Enforcement Jon Connor and Public Works Director Kevin Gagne 
made a presentation to the Council about the new Casella Cart to Curb program and the language 
in City Ordinances that the vendor cannot pick up from mixed use properties such as residences 
with a small business. They plan to bring an ordinance amendment proposal to the Council at the 
next meeting. 
 
UPDATE FROM THE LEWISTON HOUSING AUTHORITY 
 
Executive Director Chris Kilmurry provided updates on their projects – Choice Neighborhood 
Wedgewood is operating; DeWitt is close to opening.  There will be commercial entities on the 
first floor. Martel Phase 1 should open July 2027.  Martel Phase 2 plan s are complete. Martel 
Phase 3 will be submitted to the state in July. Soliel 1 & 2 on Ash Street – plans are 90% 
complete, there will be 72 units of family housing. Demolishing Lafayette Terrace and Maple 
Knoll soon. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
No members of the public spoke at this time. 
 
REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
Councilor Martel – Bates students are back in town, need to show accountability, causing noise 
and nuisance problems for area residents close to campus. 
 
Councilor Nagine – Apologized to Councilor Martel – his comments in a recent email were not 
professional or civil, and he reacted poorly. 
 
Councilor Harriman – Asked to have an update from the Public Safety Committee.  Councilor 
Longchamps noted their third committee meeting was this afternoon and their work is going 
well.  
Councilor Roy – Asked about the power outlet issue at the Art Walk. The Deputy City 
Administrator noted L/A Arts did not request power until late Friday afternoon and it was too 
late for Public Works to hook it up, it is a communication misunderstanding that is has since 
been resolved. 
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
Mayor – Be sure to watch America’s Got Talent and vote for Issac Atkins of Lewiston. 
 
Councilor Nagine – Would like information on email etiquette and FOAA limits.
CITY COUNCIL  SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
                             
9 
 
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
Councilor Martel stated the discussion with the City Attorney should take place in public session 
and not in a confidential session. 
 
VOTE (319-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To enter into an Executive Session pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405(6) (A) and (E) to discuss 
a legal matter with the City Attorney.   Did Not Pass - Vote 4-3 (Councilors Roy, Martel and 
Longchamps opposed) 
 
Note – Per Maine state statutes, a 3/5th vote of the Council (minimum of 5 affirmative votes) is 
required to enter an executive session.  
  
 
VOTE (320-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To adjourn at 8:55 P.M.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Kathleen M. Montejo, MMC  
City Clerk 
Lewiston, Maine
